artworks.title: The Pleiades
artworks.description: Vedder's seven star-sisters include Alcyone — the Pleiad whose name also labels the cluster's brightest star. Not Alcyone wife of Ceyx, nor the Giant Alcyoneus.

artworks.title: The Dance of the Pleiades (Star Lore of All Ages, plate)
artworks.description: Olcott's plate after Vedder: Alcyone among the dancers — the Pleiad Poseidon loved, mother of Hyrieus in some catalogues.

artworks.title: Study for "The Pleiades"
artworks.description: MET study for the Pleiades canvas — Alcyone as one face of the Seven Sisters before they harden into paint and star-names.

artworks.title: The Rising of the Pleiades (illustration to Hesiod)
artworks.description: Flaxman on Hesiod's calendar: the Pleiades rise — Alcyone's cluster as the sign for reaping, not the halcyon bird of Ceyx.

popCulture.title: Alcyone (Pleiad)
popCulture.description: One of the seven Pleiades; brightest star of the cluster bears her name — distinct from Alcyone of Trachis and from the Giant Alcyoneus.

popCulture.title: Pleiades (Greek mythology)
popCulture.description: Atlas' and Pleione's daughters — Alcyone among the seven transformed into the winter stars.
